notes: The Arduino UNO R4 WiFi is not in the catalogue (only the UNO R3 is), so I added it as a new part type with the UNO's port names.

The breadboard in the image has rows j-f in the top half and e-a in the bottom half. The catalogue calls the top half bank 't' (rows a-e) and the bottom half bank 'b' (rows f-j). I used the row letters printed on the image. Rows a-e are therefore bank 't' and rows f-j are bank 'b'.
Rail hole numbers are estimated from the picture. Rail row bn is the one beside the black line and bp is the one beside the red line.
The 5V wire goes to rail bp, and the GND wire goes to rail bn.
The potentiometer is a blue trimmer. Its two outer legs sit in columns 13 and 15 (row e). The wiper leg sits in column 14 on the other side of the centre gap (row f).
A red jumper takes 5V from rail bp to column 13, which is the potentiometer VCC leg. A black jumper takes column 15, the GND leg, to rail bn.
The yellow A5 wire goes to the potentiometer wiper at column 14 (row j).
The buzzer legs are in columns 26 and 30 (row e). Column 26 is the positive leg. The yellow A0 (DAC) wire goes to column 26 and a black jumper takes column 30 to the GND rail.
The tutorial text does not describe the wiring. The circuit image is the authority, and I took the connections from it.
